decisions.decision: Add the six Enterprise stages and the two Renewal-only stages to the OpportunityStage StandardValueSet as a full merge of the org's currently active values, not as a partial file listing only the new ones.
decisions.rationale: automation-selection.md, flow-pattern-selector.md and sharing-selection.md were each read end to end; none of them routes a picklist-value deploy, and standards/decision-trees/README.md lists no tree that does. The skill reference is the source: section 3 states that the deactivate-by-omission rule of api_meta.txt:47482-47483 applies to StandardValueSet too, 'so a partial file is a mass deactivation'. That single sentence is what turns an obvious-looking file into a decision.
alternatives_rejected: Ship only the eight new values and let the platform merge them
Create the stages in Setup by hand and deploy nothing
Use a GlobalValueSet instead of the standard value set
decisions.consequences: The build cannot produce the deployable file offline: the union needs the org's current list. M1-S01's deploy-order.md leads with the retrieve, assumption A24 carries the risk at high, and the M1 gate has a manual tick on the diff.

decisions.decision: Two Sales Processes bound to two Record Types, rather than one wide process exposing all ten stages to both motions.
decisions.rationale: No decision tree routes between one process and many; the trade is documented in the skill, which names the single-catch-all process as anti-pattern 1 - it 'forces every record type to expose all stages, including irrelevant ones for that motion' and makes forecast rollups unreliable. Q36's default said the same. The Path constraint settles what was left: only one PathAssistant may exist per record type per object, so two guidance sets require two record types whatever the stage lists did.
alternatives_rejected: One Sales Process with all ten stages
Two processes on one record type
A picklist filter instead of a BusinessProcess
decisions.consequences: Two record types means two layouts, two Paths, two recordTypeVisibilities rows and a layout assignment that only a Profile can carry - which is why M2-S02 exists and why it is human-gated.

decisions.decision: Enforce the 20% discount cap with a Validation Rule carrying a $Permission bypass, not with a record-triggered Flow or Apex.
decisions.rationale: automation-selection.md was read end to end and the requirements-clarifier had already filed the same finding: the tree's scope is six automation engines and Validation Rule is not one of them, so its Q-tree has no branch that reaches this choice and citing Q2 or Q3 would be a fabricated ground. The skill reference carries it instead: its Example 1 is a discount-shaped Opportunity rule with the bypass clause first inside the AND, which is the exact shape M2-S03 ships.
alternatives_rejected: Before-save record-triggered Flow raising a fault
Apex before-update trigger
Layout-level Required on Discount__c
decisions.consequences: The rule fires on every save path including the API, which Q42's default asked for. It also means the only escape is the Custom Permission, so the bypass permission set becomes a human-gated access step and every use has to be recorded by hand (Q17).

decisions.decision: Manager sign-off is a declarative Approval Process with a record lock and an approval history, not a Flow approval or a custom Apex approval object.
decisions.rationale: automation-selection.md's numbered tree does not reach Approval Process at all - Q1's trigger list has no option for 'a business decision needing one person's sign-off' - and its only mention is an unnumbered cheat-sheet row, 'Approval chain | Approval Process -> Flow post-approval | Flow with branching | Apex custom approval'. A row is not a branch, so no branch id is cited and the skill carries the decision. Q3's requirement clauses - outcome and comments on the record, locked while pending - are what the native engine gives and a Flow would have to re-implement.
alternatives_rejected: Screen Flow approval with a custom status field
Apex custom approval records
Chatter approval post
decisions.consequences: Record locking, approval history and the approver hierarchy come free, but process ORDER is not in the metadata and has to be set in Setup after deploy (assumption A34), and the rejection comments cannot be quoted in the email (assumption A27).

decisions.decision: The Submit-for-approval control is an LWC calling imperative Apex, not a Screen Flow quick action.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q8. Can the action complete in under 10s without custom UI?
    ├── Yes  → Screen Flow with Quick Action OR simple Headless Quick Action (Flow)
    └── No   → LWC calling imperative Apex (see templates/lwc/patterns/imperativeApexPattern.js)
decisions.rationale: Q1's 'a user clicking a button or filling a form' reaches Q7; Q7's 'Yes (record page)' reaches Q8. Q8's condition is a conjunction - under 10s AND without custom UI - and requirement.md item 4 asks for custom UI in so many words: a component that shows the discount and the approval status alongside a button whose enabled state is a rule. The submit itself would finish well inside 10s, so it is the custom-UI half that makes the answer No, and the No leaf names the component and the template it should be built from.
alternatives_rejected: Screen Flow with a Quick Action
Headless Quick Action (Flow)
The standard Submit for Approval action on the layout
decisions.consequences: An LWC and an Apex controller put this build under a 75% Apex coverage gate it would not otherwise have, which is why M3-S03 ships a test class and why M3-S04 ships a Jest suite.

decisions.decision: The LWC entry point (@AuraEnabled) and the Flow-invocable action (@InvocableMethod) are separate classes over one service class, rather than one class carrying both annotations.
decisions.rationale: Q34's answer calls for an invocable Apex action, and an LWC can only import an @AuraEnabled method - so the obvious shape is one method carrying both. The gotcha forbids it in the guide's own words: 'The only annotation that can be used with the InvocableMethod annotation is Deprecated' (apexdev L5430), and 'Only one method in a class can have the InvocableMethod annotation' (L5422), with the remedy stated as 'One action per outer class; share the body through a service.' No decision tree routes an annotation choice.
alternatives_rejected: One class with @AuraEnabled and @InvocableMethod on the same method
One class with both annotations on different methods
Drop the invocable and expose only @AuraEnabled
decisions.consequences: Three classes plus a test rather than one. check_invocable_methods.py's IM001 is the regression guard - it was run against a deliberately broken copy of this step's own output and fired CRITICAL at exit 1, so the test on M3-S03 is known to be live rather than vacuous.

decisions.decision: Manager visibility of their own reps' Enterprise pipeline is left to the existing role hierarchy: no org-wide default change, no sharing rule, no Apex managed sharing.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q2. Is U in the same role or above the record owner's role in the hierarchy?
    ├── Yes, and "Grant access using hierarchies" is ON  → Access already granted; done
    ├── Yes, but hierarchy is disabled on T              → Q3
    └── No                                               → Q3
decisions.rationale: Q24's answer states the mechanism outright - 'Each manager sees only their own reps' pipeline on the report (role hierarchy does that)' - and Q4 ruled out any sharing change. Reading the tree from START with U = an Enterprise manager and the record owner = one of their reps, Q2's first leaf is the terminal answer: the manager is above the owner in the hierarchy and hierarchy access is on, so the access already exists and no later layer is needed. Q1 was read first and is not the branch that resolves this - it only routes on the current OWD, which this build does not change.
alternatives_rejected: Criteria-based sharing rule on RecordTypeId
Opportunity teams
Tightening the Opportunity OWD
decisions.consequences: The dashboard is the one place this does not hold: Q24 asked for the full pipeline on the tile, so it runs as a SpecifiedUser and every viewer sees the VP's access level regardless of their own - which is why M4-S02 is human-gated and why assumption A29 exists.

decisions.decision: The approval process's entry criteria is a formula (Discount__c > 0.20), not a criteriaItems row comparing to 20.
decisions.rationale: A Percent field carries the fraction in formula context and the plain number outside it: 'percent fields are expressed divided by 100 in formulas (100% is expressed as 1; 50% is expressed as 0.5)', and the same gotcha spells out that a Decision comparing the field directly is on the other path and must be bounded with > 50 rather than > 0.5. Only the formula half is grounded in this library. entryCriteria takes criteriaItems OR formula and never both, so choosing the formula puts the threshold in the one representation the corpus settles - and makes it identical to the validation rule's, which is what a reader of both files will expect.
alternatives_rejected: criteriaItems on Opportunity.Discount__c greaterThan 20
criteriaItems greaterThan 0.20
A formula field holding the boolean
decisions.consequences: The component's design attribute stays 20 because it reads the UI API rather than a formula, so the two representations coexist in one build. The Jest suite pins the component's reading, and assumption A35 makes the divergence a deploy-order check rather than a surprise.

decisions.decision: The approval process ships active true, overriding the deploy-inactive guidance its own skill gives for a production deploy.
decisions.rationale: Grounded on the two places in this library that state the Active requirement itself. admin/approval-process-apex-patterns/references/metadata-examples.md lines 49-53: '<active>true</active> - required field. The ProcessDefinition preflight query below asserts State = Active; an inactive process is invisible to a submission that names it.' And the same skill's templates/approval-process-apex-patterns-template.md line 30, the preflight row: 'Is the process State = Active? | | A named submission to an inactive process fails'. M3-S03's Apex passes the bare developer name Discount_Approval to setProcessDefinitionNameOrId, so what this build ships is exactly the named submission both lines describe. The deploy-inactive guidance in the same file at lines 515-517 - 'A production process should deploy inactive and be activated after its workflow actions and templates exist' - is written for a SPLIT deploy; this build ships the two workflow alerts, the four field updates, the three email templates and the process in one package, so the condition that guidance waits for is already met at deploy time. Overriding published production guidance is still an accepted risk rather than a neutral choice: assumption A36 records it and it carries the process-order prerequisite A34. Correction to plan v1, which cited gotcha 14 for this: that citation was wrong. Gotcha 14's subject is a NULL processDefinitionNameOrId routing by org process order, which is the opposite case, and it says nothing about a named process requiring State Active. The citation is replaced here rather than the conclusion re-argued.
alternatives_rejected: Ship active false and activate by hand
Ship active false and have the Apex omit setProcessDefinitionNameOrId
Ship two packages
decisions.consequences: Process order still has to be set in Setup - the metadata carries no order - which is assumption A34 and a line in M3-S02's deploy-order.md. The Apex is unaffected either way because it names the process explicitly. Filed for the library and NOT for this build to resolve: admin/approval-process-apex-patterns contradicts itself on this point. Its prose at references/metadata-examples.md:515-517 says a production process should deploy inactive, while its own checker at scripts/check_approval_process_apex_patterns.py:376-386 raises HIGH on <active>false</active> whenever Apex in the same tree names the process - and cites gotcha 14 for a rule gotcha 14 does not state. No plan can satisfy both halves of one skill. This build follows the checker and the two sources above that do state the Active requirement, and records the disagreement as a library defect for the depth-wave worklist rather than resolving it in a build plan.

decisions.decision: The record page's org-default assignment ships as actionOverrides on objects/Opportunity/Opportunity.object-meta.xml inside the same step as the FlexiPage, rather than on the object-model step.
decisions.rationale: A FlexiPage carries no assignment of its own; the org default lives in an actionOverrides block on the object file, one per formFactor. check_lightning_record_page_configuration.py reads object files with objects/*/*.object-meta.xml relative to --manifest-dir and does not recurse, so the override and the page have to sit in one step directory or the assignment check cannot run at all. Run against this plan's M3-S05 fixture it went from four ERRORs and exit 1 to 'No errors found' and exit 0 once the override and the three component identifiers were added.
alternatives_rejected: Put actionOverrides on the object-model step
Assign the page by hand in Lightning App Builder
Assign it through an application file
decisions.consequences: It bends build-planner Step 6 rule 6, which says object-level children belong to the object-model step. Nothing collides - M1-S01 writes the decomposed recordTypes, businessProcesses and fields files and no Opportunity.object-meta.xml at all - but the tension between that rule and a non-recursive checker is real and is filed as driver's-log material. An app with its own Opportunity record page still wins over the org default (assumption A38).

inputs.error_message: A discount above 20% needs manager approval before this opportunity can be Closed Won - submit for approval from the Discount panel.
inputs.note: Formula shape, in force order per admin/validation-rules/references/metadata-examples.md Example 1: NOT($Permission.Bypass_Opportunity_Sales_Validation) first, then the record-type relevance gate (RecordType.DeveloperName compared with = because DeveloperName is text, never ISPICKVAL), then the stage test, then the business condition. The threshold is 0.20 and not 20: D8 and assumption A35 record why - a Percent field is expressed divided by 100 in formula context. Approval_Status__c is tested with ISPICKVAL rather than ISBLANK applied to the picklist, which is exactly what VR-PICK-01 exists to catch (assumption A10). errorMessage is Q15's wording at 129 characters, inside the 255 limit, with the em dash written as a hyphen so the file needs no entity escaping. inputs.feature_summary: Submit exactly one Enterprise or Renewal Opportunity into the Discount_Approval process from a record-page button and return the outcome to the component inline
inputs.note: Three classes plus a test, for the reason D6 records: an LWC can only import an @AuraEnabled method, and @AuraEnabled cannot be stacked on an @InvocableMethod - 'The only annotation that can be used with the InvocableMethod annotation is Deprecated'. So OpportunityApprovalService holds the body, OpportunityApprovalController is the @AuraEnabled entry point, OpportunityApprovalSubmitAction holds the single @InvocableMethod, and the test targets the service. Template closure was checked before this step was written: the only templates/apex/** file cited is tests/TestDataFactory.cls, which greps clean for other template classes and for __c/__mdt tokens, so it ships verbatim with its meta XML in this same step and needs no Apex-foundations step. SecurityUtils and ApplicationLogger are deliberately NOT cited - SecurityUtils references ApplicationLogger, which references Application_Log__c with eight fields and Logger_Setting__mdt with one, a closure no step in this plan ships - so the service enforces access with WITH USER_MODE on its single SOQL instead, which is the read idiom for a 62.0 class. setProcessDefinitionNameOrId takes the bare developer name 'Discount_Approval': check_approval_process_apex_patterns.py resolved that string against Opportunity.Discount_Approval.approvalProcess-meta.xml in a fixture run, which is how the form was settled rather than by choosing between the two skills' differing examples. The shipped TestDataFactory.cls-meta.xml carries <apiVersion>67.0</apiVersion> - the canonical template's own value - beside the four authored classes at 62.0, because section 4's Apex row note requires the template to ship as a verbatim copy WITH its meta XML and a rewritten apiVersion would no longer be verbatim. Mixed api versions in one deploy are legal; what the split changes is the read idiom, and AGENT_CONTRACT's Apex security table makes WITH USER_MODE correct for the 62.0 authored classes while 67.0 enforces user mode by default - so the factory needs no keyword and the service states one. The manual test below now pins the version as well as the diff. No deploy-order.md is declared either, and that is the deliberate half of a real tension: agents/apex-builder/AGENT.md Output Contract deliverable 2 names deploy-order.md as where a shipped template class's provenance is recorded, while agents/build-planner/AGENT.md Step 6 rule 3 says an apex-builder step declares its .cls / .trigger files and their meta XML and nothing else. Rule 3 is followed; the provenance claim is carried by the manual test below plus M4-S04's runbook, which is the second of the two remedies the verifier named. No package.xml is declared either - see the manifest test.

Step scope: the invocable contract is entirely inside this step's classes. One INFO remains on the Automation row ('no automation choice to cite - artefact is configuration') and never affects the exit code. Exit policy: bare - any ERROR fails and there is no severity flag. Empty/missing file: 'file not found' at exit 1.

scope build is declared because the command's --manifest-dir already reads the whole artefacts tree: the matrix is checked against every step's components, not against this step's own directory. Both flags are declared together and each does a different job - under --manifest-dir discovery alone a missing matrix is an INFO at exit 0, while under --file a missing path prints 'does not exist (or is not a file). Nothing was validated.' and exits 1, so the --file half is what makes an absent document a failure. Fixture run over a two-row build-schema matrix printed '0 coverage gap(s), 0 orphan(s), 0 error(s)' at exit 0; the same matrix with untyped artefact names raised two WARNs, 'artefact has no metadata type - write <MetadataType>:<ApiName>', which is why every row here carries the type prefix. Exit policy: lenient, with --strict promoting WARNs; not passed, because the orphan WARN is how an incomplete matrix reports itself rather than how it fails. A row whose status is In Build with no artefact and no test id is an ERROR at exit 1.

--manifest-dir rather than --file, deliberately: the flag makes the checker read the case pack and the criteria document together, so every ac_id is resolved. Fixture evidence - a three-case pack alone printed 'OK - 3 case(s), 0 run-sheet row(s), no criteria file present so ac_id resolution was skipped'; the same pack beside acceptance-criteria.md printed 'OK - 3 case(s), 0 run-sheet row(s), 3 criterion id(s) cross-checked'. Both exit 0, and only the second is a real check. Required per case: case_id, ac_id, req_id, persona, sandbox, steps, evidence and pass_rule, with no persona naming System Administrator, and at least one negative_path case per req_id - a two-case fixture missing the negative for REQ-001 failed with 'no case is marked negative - every requirement needs at least one case that proves the feature blocks the wrong action' at exit 1. Exit policy: lenient, --strict promotes warnings; not passed.

--manifest-dir rather than --file, which is the standard form this checker does accept and which keeps this line clear of validate's non-standard-argument-form WARN. It scans recursively and lints only what looks like a criteria document: over a fixture directory holding all four of this step's outputs it printed 'Checking: .../acceptance-criteria.md' then '1 document(s) checked - 0 error(s), 0 warning(s).' and exited 0, ignoring the workbook, the matrix and the YAML pack. What it enforces was learned the hard way on that fixture: a Then clause describing a blocked save without quoting the message failed with 'Then-fails clause has no exact error message in quotes and no # TBD marker' at exit 1, so every negative criterion here quotes the validation rule's errorMessage verbatim. Note the file must carry a 'Scenario:' header, an acceptance_criteria: YAML record or a criteria table - a folder with none of those exits 2 on nothing to lint, so this exit code is only meaningful because check-outputs confirms acceptance-criteria.md exists and is non-empty first. Exit policy: bare on ERROR; warnings never fail the run.

inputs.note: The one manifest that carries every member, including the ones no step declares a manifest for: M3-S03's five ApexClass members and M3-S04's LightningComponentBundle member, per section 5's Apex exception and section 4's borrowed-agent condition 2. requirement.summary: Build a standalone Enterprise + Renewal Opportunity sales process for Northwind (12 reps, 2 managers, 1 sales-ops admin): two Sales Processes with staged probabilities and Path checklists, opportunity products against the Standard Price Book with a before-Propose product gate and a 20% discount cap enforced by validation rules, a formal manager approval process with record lock for over-cap discounts, a small record-page LWC (discount, approval status, Submit for approval) backed by an Apex invocable action, an open-pipeline report and a close-month dashboard tile, and two record types — all without touching the existing SMB process, and with no integration or data migration in scope.

clarifications.question: Walk me through the last Enterprise deal you lost at Propose or Negotiate — what actually happened first?
clarifications.why: Stated exit criteria are aspirational; loss narratives expose the gate that actually existed (requirements-gathering Gotcha 10 / sales-process-mapping).
clarifications.answer_shape: One rewritten exit criterion per stage where the current wording is aspirational, plus the field it makes required.
clarifications.proposed_default: Today: one generic pipeline (the requirement states this); no stage-specific exit criteria exist yet for Enterprise deals, so no loss narrative is on file.
clarifications.answer: The last two losses at Negotiate were price: legal and procurement pushed for discounts we could not give without a manager, and the rep had already verbally promised. That is exactly why the discount cap and approval must be on the record, not in email.

clarifications.question: Who is allowed to move a deal into Negotiate, and who actually does today?
clarifications.why: The platform allows backward and skipped stage moves silently — only a validation rule stops it.
clarifications.answer_shape: The owner per stage transition, and either a validation-rule row or an explicit decision not to enforce stage order.
clarifications.answer: Only the rep who owns the deal moves it to Negotiate, and only after the manager has seen the proposal; today reps move it whenever they like. The exit checklist should say: proposal sent, decision-maker identified, discount within policy or approval submitted.

clarifications.question: When an Enterprise or Renewal deal closes, who has to know, and what do they need from the record?
clarifications.why: Closed Won exit obligations (onboarding case, contract, booking) get built by nobody unless they are named as stage requirements.
clarifications.answer_shape: The Sales → Service and Sales → Finance handoff rows and the fields each needs; the requirement is silent on this.
clarifications.answer: Finance needs the closed-won amount, products, discount and close date; Customer Success needs the account, products and contract start; both read the record — no notification build in scope, the report covers it.

clarifications.question: Must the SMB team be unable to see Enterprise pipeline (and vice versa), or is this purely a process-guidance separation?
clarifications.why: Record types and Sales Processes do not govern read access on their own — a visibility requirement routes to the sharing-selection decision tree instead.
clarifications.answer_shape: A yes/no on cross-team visibility; if yes, a `sharing_impact` value naming the layer (OWD / role hierarchy / sharing rule / team) per standards/decision-trees/sharing-selection.md.
clarifications.proposed_default: Not stated — requirement says only that the SMB process must not break, not that visibility must change.
clarifications.answer: Process-guidance separation only. SMB and Enterprise see each other's pipeline; no sharing change. The generic process stays untouched.

clarifications.question: Which forecast bucket does each of the six Enterprise stages and four Renewal stages belong in, and who signs off on that mapping?
clarifications.why: ForecastCategoryName is per-stage and the forecast rolls up by category, not by stage; two stages in the same bucket collapse the distinction the ladder was built to create.
clarifications.answer_shape: The stage-to-category table, which is the direct input to the StandardValueSet deploy.
clarifications.answer: Enterprise: Qualify=Pipeline, Discover=Pipeline, Propose=Best Case, Negotiate=Commit, Closed Won=Closed, Closed Lost=Omitted. Renewal: Renewal Review=Pipeline, Renewal Proposed=Commit, Closed Won=Closed, Closed Lost=Omitted. I (VP Sales Ops) sign off.

clarifications.question: What is the exact probability percentage for each of the six Enterprise stages and four Renewal stages?
clarifications.why: The requirement asks for "a probability" per stage but states no values; without them the stage picklist cannot be deployed.
clarifications.answer_shape: One probability value (0-100) per stage, agreed with the VP and the two managers.
clarifications.answer: Enterprise: Qualify 10, Discover 25, Propose 50, Negotiate 75, Closed Won 100, Closed Lost 0. Renewal: Renewal Review 60, Renewal Proposed 85, Closed Won 100, Closed Lost 0.

clarifications.question: Will Enterprise or Renewal opportunities ever use split credit, opportunity teams, or the Private flag?
clarifications.why: Splits are a one-way door (split types cannot be deleted through any API) and IsPrivate silently removes teams, splits and sharing from a record — none of this is mentioned in the requirement.
clarifications.answer_shape: An explicit yes/no per mechanism (splits, teams, IsPrivate), and a rule for who may set Private if it is ever allowed.
clarifications.proposed_default: Not requested — the requirement describes only reps, two managers and a sales-ops admin with no mention of splits, teams or private opportunities.
clarifications.answer: No splits, no opportunity teams, no Private flag for either process.

clarifications.question: Do Enterprise opportunities already exist on the generic record type that would need to be reassigned to the new Enterprise record type?
clarifications.why: Reassignment blanks any picklist value absent from the target record type, silently, and existing StageName values on open deals may not exist in the new picklist.
clarifications.answer_shape: The at-risk record count and the value-mapping step that must run before any reassignment.
clarifications.answer: Yes — about 140 open Enterprise deals on the generic record type. Reassign them to the Enterprise record type as a one-time data update after go-live (a runbook step, not a data-migration build); no field mapping changes.

clarifications.question: Which reports, list views, or Flow entry criteria filter on the current single Opportunity record type today?
clarifications.why: Report filters key on the label, which is not stable across a record-type change; code and Flows key on DeveloperName, which is.
clarifications.answer_shape: The rename/reassignment blast-radius list before the existing generic record type is touched or retired.
clarifications.answer: Two SMB list views and the SMB pipeline report filter on Record Type = Master today; they keep working because SMB stays on the generic record type. No Flow filters on record type.

clarifications.question: How do Enterprise deals actually get closed — a rep in the UI, a manager doing a bulk edit, or a data load?
clarifications.why: Close-path assumptions decide whether a validation rule is sufficient enforcement of the discount cap and product requirement.
clarifications.answer_shape: The enforcement mechanism confirmed per rule rather than assumed by reflex.
clarifications.proposed_default: Rep in the UI, one record at a time (12 reps, no integration and no migration per the requirement).
clarifications.answer: A rep in the UI, always. Managers never bulk-edit stages; no data loads close deals.

clarifications.question: Of the "key fields per stage" the requirement asks for, which must be filled in before the rep can advance, versus merely shown for context?
clarifications.why: Path displays; it does not enforce. The must-fill list is a validation-rule backlog, not a Path backlog, and the requirement does not separate the two.
clarifications.answer_shape: A per-stage list split into must-fill (feeds admin/validation-rules) and shown-only fields.
clarifications.answer: Required to advance: Qualify→Discover: Amount and Close Date; Discover→Propose: at least one product and Next Step; Propose→Negotiate: Primary Contact (Contact role Decision Maker) and Discount; Negotiate→Closed Won: Discount approved if above 20%. Shown for context only: Lead Source, Type.

clarifications.question: Does the discount live on the Opportunity itself (a rollup or a header field) or only on the OpportunityLineItem records?
clarifications.why: Validation rules don't fire on an Opportunity when only a child OpportunityLineItem changes; a rule guarding a header-level discount field never runs if the actual edit happens on the line item.
clarifications.answer_shape: The object the discount field lives on, or a decision to use a record-triggered flow on OpportunityLineItem instead of (or alongside) an Opportunity-level validation rule.
clarifications.answer: A header field on the Opportunity: Discount__c (percent), typed by the rep as the overall deal discount. Line-item discounts are not used.

clarifications.question: Which users or integrations must be able to save an Enterprise/Renewal opportunity the product-count or discount-cap rule would otherwise reject?
clarifications.why: Every rule with no bypass blocks every data load and every API write that does not meet the condition, including the sales-ops admin doing legitimate cleanup.
clarifications.answer_shape: The Custom Permission name and the Permission Set that carries it, or a confirmed "no bypass" decision.
clarifications.proposed_default: The sales-ops admin profile, via a Custom Permission bypass (per admin/validation-rules' own worked pattern) — no integration users, since the requirement states there are none.
clarifications.answer: Only the sales-ops admin may bypass, via a custom permission granted by a permission set; no integrations write Enterprise opportunities.

clarifications.question: Is the product-line field and the discount field confirmed to be on every layout, for every record type, that reps and managers use?
clarifications.why: errorDisplayField silently changes to Top of Page when the field isn't visible on the layout the user is looking at, which reads as a confusing error location.
clarifications.answer_shape: A confirmed layout placement per field per record type, or an error message rewritten to read correctly at the top of the page.
clarifications.answer: Discount__c will be new and must be on both new layouts; the products related list is on both. Confirm on the SMB layout nothing is added.

clarifications.question: What should the two error messages say — the product-before-Propose rule and the 20%-discount-without-approval rule — in 255 characters or fewer each, naming both the problem and the fix?
clarifications.why: errorMessage is capped at 255 characters; a rule that can't say what to do generates a support ticket per occurrence instead of a self-service fix.
clarifications.answer_shape: The final message text for each rule, not a placeholder to be filled in at deploy time.
clarifications.answer: Products rule: 'Add at least one product before moving this opportunity to Propose.' Discount rule: 'A discount above 20% needs manager approval before this opportunity can be Closed Won — submit for approval from the Discount panel.'

clarifications.question: Do any open Enterprise opportunities today already violate the future product-count or discount-cap rules?
clarifications.why: Validation rules fire on update as well as insert; an active rule on dirty data blocks every future edit of every violating record except the one edit that happens to satisfy the rule.
clarifications.answer_shape: A decision to deploy the rule with active=false plus a named cleanup owner, or a count proving the existing pipeline is already clean.
clarifications.answer: About 20 open Enterprise deals have no products and 6 have discounts above 20%; the rules apply on the next save only — no clean-up in scope.

clarifications.question: What must NOT happen automatically here, and who fixes it when the validation rule or approval process is wrong for a specific deal?
clarifications.why: "Enforce the discount cap" hides the exception path and the owner of the failure — every hard-blocking rule eventually meets a legitimate deal it should not have blocked.
clarifications.answer_shape: The exception path and a named owner — most likely the sales-ops admin bypass already asked under admin/validation-rules — confirmed as complete for both the validation rule and the approval process.
clarifications.answer: Nothing may change the Stage or Amount automatically; the approval must not auto-approve on timeout. When a rule or approval is wrong for a deal, the sales-ops admin uses the bypass permission and records why in a chatter post on the record.

clarifications.question: Walk me through what a rep does today, end to end, when closing a deal with a discount above 20% — what do they type, where, and what happens next?
clarifications.why: Stakeholders describe the workaround they built around the lack of a process as if it were the requirement; skipping this risks re-implementing today's ad hoc approval email chain rather than replacing it.
clarifications.answer_shape: An As-Is step list tagged keep/drop/replace, confirming the new validation rule and approval process fully replace whatever ad hoc practice exists today.
clarifications.proposed_default: Today: no formal cap or approval exists at all — the requirement states discounts above 20% are simply not stopped or approved today.
clarifications.answer: Today the rep emails the manager 'ok to give 25%?', the manager replies, the rep pastes the reply into the opportunity description and closes it. Nothing is enforced.

clarifications.question: Which profile does each of the 12 reps, 2 managers and the sales-ops admin actually hold?
clarifications.why: Permission sets grant record-type visibility only — the default record type and the page-layout assignment exist solely on Profile.
clarifications.answer_shape: The profile x record-type x layout matrix for all 15 users, not a per-record-type layout list.
clarifications.answer: Reps and managers: the standard Sales User profile with a Sales Cloud permission set; the sales-ops admin: System Administrator. The manager distinction is by role (Enterprise Manager role above Enterprise Rep role), not profile.

clarifications.question: Which standard fields does the platform require on the Enterprise and Renewal Opportunity layouts?
clarifications.why: A layout that omits a platform-required standard field does not deploy, and the required set is not documented in the Metadata API guide for Opportunity.
clarifications.answer_shape: The layout-required item list confirmed before the layout XML is written, rather than one --dry-run round trip per missing field.
clarifications.answer: Name, Stage, Close Date, Amount, Account Name (standard required fields); keep them on both layouts.

clarifications.question: Is the stage picklist for each process final, or still being negotiated?
clarifications.why: fieldName and recordTypeName on a PathAssistant are not updateable; re-pointing a Path after stages change is delete-and-recreate, not an edit.
clarifications.answer_shape: A yes/no on whether the stage list is locked, and if not, a decision to build the Path after the stage model settles (admin/opportunity-management).
clarifications.answer: Final as written in the requirement for both processes.

clarifications.question: Is "discount" and "approval status" read from fields on Opportunity directly, or computed/rolled up from OpportunityLineItem?
clarifications.why: The component's wire/imperative Apex call and its reactivity depend on which object and fields it reads; a field on the wrong object silently shows stale or blank data.
clarifications.answer_shape: The exact field API names (object + field) the component reads for discount and for approval status.
clarifications.answer: Discount__c and Approval_Status__c are fields on the Opportunity (Approval_Status__c set by the approval process: Pending, Approved, Rejected, blank). Nothing rolled up from line items.

clarifications.question: Should an Enterprise opportunity with zero related products still appear on the open-pipeline report?
clarifications.why: This decides outerJoin on the report type; an inner join makes those records invisible with no error and no empty row, which would hide exactly the deals the product-before-Propose rule is meant to catch early.
clarifications.answer_shape: The report-type decision, and whether an existing Opportunity report type can be reused or a custom one is needed.
clarifications.proposed_default: Yes, it should still appear — the report is meant to show open pipeline by stage, including deals that have not yet reached Propose.
clarifications.answer: Yes, show it — with the product count column so the manager sees the gap.

clarifications.question: Should the two managers each see only their own reps' opportunities on the report and dashboard, or the full Enterprise pipeline?
clarifications.why: This is the dashboardType (SpecifiedUser vs LoggedInUser) decision; SpecifiedUser shows one person's data to everyone, LoggedInUser shows each viewer their own slice.
clarifications.answer_shape: The running-user decision, and a named non-human service user if SpecifiedUser is chosen.
clarifications.answer: Each manager sees only their own reps' pipeline on the report (role hierarchy does that); the dashboard tile shows the full Enterprise pipeline as the running user (the VP).

clarifications.question: Who besides the two managers and the VP is allowed to see these rows, and who may open the report/dashboard folder?
clarifications.why: Folder access and record access are separate layers; View on the folder only grants the right to run the report, not to see every row in it.
clarifications.answer_shape: The folder accessType + folderShares design, and whether record-level sharing needs to change as well.
clarifications.proposed_default: The two Enterprise managers, the VP, and the sales-ops admin; reps do not need folder access per the requirement ("Managers need a report...").
clarifications.answer: The two managers, the VP, and the sales-ops admin. The folder is shared to the Enterprise Managers public group (managers + VP) with View; the admin manages it.

clarifications.question: Is the Opportunity report type's exact API name (and the column codes for Stage, Amount and the discount field) confirmed from a retrieve against this org, rather than assumed?
clarifications.why: Standard report type API names are not always the object name, and report column codes are report-type-specific; a plausible-looking guess is rejected only at deploy time with no offline way to confirm it.
clarifications.answer_shape: The confirmed report-type API name and column codes as they appear in a retrieved report on this org, with an honest gap noted for anything that could not be harvested (this build is design-only, with no org connection to retrieve against).
clarifications.answer: No — confirm the report type name and column codes from a retrieve during the build; never guess them (we learned that on another project).

clarifications.question: Who may submit the approval request — the rep only, or also the sales-ops admin on the rep's behalf?
clarifications.why: allowedSubmitters is required and typed (owner, creator, user, group, role, ...); leaving it at owner-only silently excludes anyone who submits on behalf of a rep. If the Apex invocable action calls setSubmitterId, that id must itself be in allowedSubmitters or the call is rejected.
clarifications.answer_shape: The allowedSubmitters block, confirmed against who the requirement names as doing the submitting, and against the identity the Apex action will submit as.
clarifications.proposed_default: The record owner (rep) and the two managers; the requirement does not mention the sales-ops admin submitting on a rep's behalf.
clarifications.answer: The rep only. The sales-ops admin may submit on the rep's behalf only via the bypass path, and that is exceptional.

clarifications.question: Should the rep be able to recall a submitted approval before the manager acts on it, and if so, is that admin-only or can the rep do it themselves?
clarifications.why: Approval.process with action 'Removed' (recall) is admin-only in Apex; allowRecall=false on the process narrows recall to administrators entirely, which the LWC's button state needs to reflect.
clarifications.answer_shape: A yes/no on rep-initiated recall, and if yes, the admin-context escalation the Apex action needs to perform it.
clarifications.answer: The rep may recall their own pending submission; an admin may recall any.

clarifications.question: Does the invocable Apex action ever need to submit more than one opportunity at a time, or is it always exactly one record from the LWC button click?
clarifications.why: Approval.process is DML with per-transaction limits (150 statements, 10,000 records); the invocable method's parameter shape (single vs List<Id>) and its bulk-safety design depend on the answer.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation of single-record invocation, or the chunking/bulk design if the action must ever be called for more than one record.
clarifications.proposed_default: Exactly one record per invocation, triggered by a single button click on one opportunity's record page.
clarifications.answer: Always exactly one opportunity from the button click.

clarifications.question: When Approval.process(req, false) returns a failed ProcessResult for a submission, what should the rep see, and does anyone besides the rep need to know?
clarifications.why: allOrNone=false returns per-row ProcessResults that nothing reads unless the Apex action writes a handler for them; the LWC also needs a defined error shape to show the rep something more useful than a generic toast.
clarifications.answer_shape: The error surface (an inline message on the LWC, a toast, or both) and whether a failed submission is logged or alerted anywhere beyond the rep's screen.
clarifications.answer: The rep sees the failure reason inline in the component (toast + text); nobody else needs to know; the failure is not logged anywhere else.

clarifications.question: While an opportunity is pending approval, may the current approver (the manager) edit the record, or only an admin?
clarifications.why: recordEditability is AdminOnly or AdminOrCurrentApprover; the record is locked otherwise, and the requirement says only "the opportunity is locked while pending" without naming who, if anyone, may still edit it.
clarifications.answer_shape: The chosen enum value, and a named exception process for in-flight corrections if AdminOnly is chosen.
clarifications.proposed_default: AdminOnly — the requirement's wording ("locked while pending") reads as a hard lock, with the sales-ops admin as the only exception path for corrections.
clarifications.answer: Only an admin may edit while pending; the manager approves or rejects, they do not edit.

clarifications.question: Who is the approver on each Enterprise/Renewal opportunity — the rep's direct manager via role/user hierarchy, or a fixed named approver?
clarifications.why: Approver type is adhoc, user, userHierarchyField, relatedUserField, or queue; userHierarchyField only works if nextAutomatedApprover is declared, and a blank hierarchy field is a runtime submission failure, not a design-time error.
clarifications.answer_shape: The approver type and source field, plus the fallback queue or validation rule for a rep with no manager set.
clarifications.proposed_default: The rep's manager via the standard user role/manager hierarchy (2 managers named in the requirement), assuming the hierarchy field is populated for all 12 reps.
clarifications.answer: The rep's direct manager through the user hierarchy (Manager field on the user), which matches the role hierarchy.

clarifications.question: What should happen automatically on submit, approve, reject and recall — an email alert to the manager and the rep, a field update on an Approval_Status__c field the LWC reads, or both?
clarifications.why: Approval actions are workflow action references (Alert, FieldUpdate, Task) that live in a separate workflow metadata file, not in the approval file; a referenced alert or field update that is missing fails the deploy, and the LWC's "approval status" display needs a field the approval process actually updates.
clarifications.answer_shape: The action inventory per event (submit/approve/reject/recall), including the field the LWC will read for "approval status", and confirmation those actions exist before the approval process is built.
clarifications.answer: Submit: email to the manager, Approval_Status__c = Pending, record locked. Approve: email to the rep, Approval_Status__c = Approved, record unlocked. Reject: email to the rep with the comments, Approval_Status__c = Rejected, unlocked. Recall: Approval_Status__c cleared, unlocked, no email.

clarifications.question: When the "Submit for approval" button is enabled — discount > 20% and not already pending/approved — should clicking it call an invocable Apex action that wraps Approval.process(), or should it navigate the rep to the standard Submit for Approval action?
clarifications.why: Process.submit cannot be called directly from LWC; it requires an Apex invocable method, which is a distinct build artefact (its own class, its own test) from the component itself, and the requirement asks for a button embedded in a small custom component rather than a link to the standard action.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation of the mechanism (Apex invocable vs standard-action navigation) and, if Apex, the class name and its test plan.
clarifications.proposed_default: An invocable Apex action wrapping Approval.process(), called imperatively from the LWC on button click, so the component can show a confirmation/error inline rather than navigating away.
clarifications.answer: Call an invocable Apex action (one record) that submits the standard approval process and returns the outcome; the component refreshes the record after submit. No Flow screen.

clarifications.question: How will the enable/disable logic for the Submit button be tested — what Jest stubs and what Apex test class are expected as acceptance evidence?
clarifications.why: The sfdx-lwc-jest lightning-stubs fire no events and do not reflect every property as a DOM attribute; a test asserting getAttribute() on the button's disabled state can pass for the wrong reason.
clarifications.answer_shape: A test plan naming the properties set/read on the stub and the events dispatched, plus the Apex test class covering the invocable action's bulk and negative-path behaviour.
clarifications.answer: Jest: button disabled when Discount__c <= 20 or Approval_Status__c in (Pending, Approved); enabled otherwise — stub the wire with getRecord data. Apex: a test class for the invocable that asserts the ProcessInstance exists after submit and that a second submit while pending returns the failure message.

clarifications.question: Do Enterprise and Renewal run genuinely different stage sequences, confirming two Sales Processes are needed?
clarifications.why: Two sequences means two Sales Processes, and businessProcess is required on an Opportunity record type.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation plus the record-type count, which is the largest cost line in the handoff brief.
clarifications.proposed_default: Yes — the requirement names two distinct stage lists (Qualify..Closed Lost vs Renewal Review..Closed Lost), so two Sales Processes and two Record Types are required.

clarifications.question: What does the board pack call each forecast bucket for Enterprise and Renewal deals?
clarifications.why: Only the documented ForecastCategoryName values exist as platform values; a mismatched internal label creates a silent forecast-rollup gap.
clarifications.answer_shape: The internal-label to platform-value translation table, or a decision to hold a separate forecast session.
clarifications.proposed_default: Standard ForecastCategoryName values (Pipeline, Best Case, Commit, Closed) mapped one-to-one to the stages named in the requirement, pending sign-off.

clarifications.question: Does any integration or Apex write Probability or ForecastCategoryName directly on an Enterprise or Renewal opportunity?
clarifications.why: Both fields are overridable per record, and a StageName update in the same transaction silently overwrites the override.
clarifications.answer_shape: A confirmed empty list of writers, or the list to fix before the ladder ships.
clarifications.proposed_default: No — the requirement states no integrations exist or are being added.

clarifications.question: How will Enterprise/Renewal stage movement be measured six months from now?
clarifications.why: Stage history cannot be backfilled, and OpportunityHistory is not itself a stage-history table.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation that history tracking is switched on at deploy time, and the report/query chosen up front.
clarifications.proposed_default: Field history tracking enabled on StageName from day one; reporting uses OpportunityFieldHistory / OpportunityHistory as appropriate.

clarifications.question: Which picklist values differ between the Enterprise and Renewal processes, field by field, beyond StageName?
clarifications.why: If nothing else differs, a second record type is warranted purely by StageName/businessProcess, which the requirement already implies; if something else differs, that becomes an additional picklistValues block.
clarifications.answer_shape: The full picklistValues block per record type, and confirmation no other field needs to differ.
clarifications.proposed_default: StageName is confirmed to differ (from the requirement); no other differing picklist is named.

clarifications.question: Are Person Accounts enabled on this org?
clarifications.why: Person Account record types are a separate model and the Metadata API will not round-trip their custom picklist values; this changes the record-type build.
clarifications.answer_shape: A confirmed no, or a separate design track and manual verification step if yes.
clarifications.proposed_default: No — the requirement describes an Enterprise B2B sales process with no mention of Person Accounts.

clarifications.question: Is the "at least one product line before Propose" rule meant to be enforced everywhere (API, every layout, Flow), or only on the standard UI?
clarifications.why: Layout Required binds to that layout only — API, Flow and every other layout ignore it, so a layout-level control alone would not meet the requirement's wording.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation that this is a validation-rule decision, not a layout-required decision.
clarifications.proposed_default: Enforced everywhere via a validation rule, not a layout-Required setting, since the requirement says the opportunity "cannot move to Propose" without qualification.

clarifications.question: Is any workflow field update or other legacy automation writing to StageName, Amount or the discount field after save on Enterprise/Renewal opportunities?
clarifications.why: Custom validation rules are not re-run after a workflow field update re-saves the record, so the rule would not be a database invariant if one exists.
clarifications.answer_shape: Either a migration of any such field update to a before-save flow, or an explicit acceptance that violating records can exist.
clarifications.proposed_default: No — the requirement describes a net-new process with no existing automation named on these fields.

clarifications.question: Does the discount-cap formula need to read a compound field, a person name, or a dependent picklist?
clarifications.why: Validation rules cannot use compound fields as of API version 20.0.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation the formula only touches simple number/picklist fields, or the component-field rewrite if not.
clarifications.proposed_default: No — discount is expected to be a plain percent/number field on Opportunity or OpportunityLineItem.

clarifications.question: Will the discount-cap or product-count formula need to test a picklist field (e.g. an approval-status picklist) with ISBLANK or ISNULL?
clarifications.why: The org rejects ISBLANK()/ISNULL() called directly on a picklist field at deploy time; only TEXT(<picklist>) is accepted inside those functions.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation of which fields the formula reads and that any picklist reads go through TEXT().
clarifications.proposed_default: Likely yes, if approval status is read as a picklist in the formula — NOT(ISBLANK(TEXT(Field__c))) will be used rather than the direct form.

clarifications.question: Does each of the two record types (Enterprise, Renewal) need its own Path, or does the same guidance serve both?
clarifications.why: Exactly one Path can exist per record type per object, including __Master__ — record type is the only differentiator available.
clarifications.answer_shape: The file count: one .pathAssistant-meta.xml per record type, each with a named owner.
clarifications.proposed_default: Two Paths, one per record type, since the two processes have different stage lists per the requirement.

clarifications.question: Which edition is the target org (including any sandboxes/scratch orgs used to build this)?
clarifications.why: pathAssistantEnabled defaults to true only in Enterprise Edition; a Path deploys fine into an org where Path is off and simply never renders.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation of edition, and settings/PathAssistant.settings-meta.xml included in the package instead of a manual per-org Setup step.
clarifications.proposed_default: Sales Cloud Enterprise, per the requirement — pathAssistantEnabled should default on, but the settings file should still ship to make it explicit.

clarifications.question: Does anyone need to see the Path guidance without clicking to expand it?
clarifications.why: The Path loads collapsed unless canOverrideAutoPathCollapseWithUserPref is true (default false in every edition).
clarifications.answer_shape: A decision on the org-wide expand preference before rep adoption of the checklist is measured.

clarifications.question: Who advances the stage — the rep in the UI, or automation?
clarifications.why: Celebration is a UI interaction reward and has no element in PathAssistant metadata at all, so it never travels with a deploy if the rep never clicks Mark Stage as Complete.
clarifications.answer_shape: Either a celebration stage the rep actually clicks through, or an honest "no celebration" decision.
clarifications.proposed_default: The rep in the UI, since the requirement describes reps working the pipeline manually with no mention of stage-advancing automation.

clarifications.question: Which Lightning record page will render the Path and the new discount/approval LWC together?
clarifications.why: The Path component is runtime_sales_pathassistant:pathAssistant in the subheader region; a page template without that region has nowhere to put it, and the requirement asks for both Path and the LWC on the same record page.
clarifications.answer_shape: The named FlexiPage that must ship in the same package as the Path and the LWC.
clarifications.proposed_default: The existing Enterprise Opportunity Lightning record page (or a new one cloned from it), confirmed to include the subheader region.

clarifications.question: Does the discount/approval component need to run anywhere besides the standard Lightning Experience record page (mobile app, an Experience Cloud site)?
clarifications.why: Container decides half the component list — lightning-datatable/tree-grid are unsupported on mobile, and only a subset of base components server-side render on an LWR site.
clarifications.answer_shape: The supportedFormFactors block for the .js-meta.xml.
clarifications.proposed_default: Lightning Experience desktop and the Salesforce mobile app only — the requirement describes reps and managers on the record page, with no Experience Cloud mention.

clarifications.question: Is the discount value ever edited inline in this component, or only ever displayed?
clarifications.why: lightning-output-field is read-only and must be a direct child of lightning-record-view-form; an editable field needs a different component shape entirely (lightning-record-edit-form or lightning-input-field).
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation the component is read-only apart from the Submit button.
clarifications.proposed_default: Displayed only — the requirement describes the component showing discount, approval status and a button, not an edit surface.

clarifications.question: Will anyone email, export, or subscribe to the open-pipeline report or the dashboard tile?
clarifications.why: Subscriptions send the running user's rows to every recipient, which interacts with the dashboardType decision above.
clarifications.answer_shape: A go/no-go on subscriptions for the two managers and the VP.

clarifications.question: Does the existing custom report type (if the pipeline report reuses one from the SMB process) already back other reports?
clarifications.why: Editing a shared custom report type reaches every report built on it; removing or adding a column removes/adds it everywhere that report type is used, which is exactly the "don't break SMB" risk named in the requirement.
clarifications.answer_shape: A blast-radius check before any existing report type is touched, or confirmation a new one is being created instead.
clarifications.proposed_default: Unknown — assume a new, Enterprise-scoped report type is built rather than editing whatever the SMB report type is, to protect the "nothing should break SMB" requirement.

clarifications.question: Is the dashboard tile's "pipeline by close month" component going to be filtered by anything else on the dashboard (e.g. by owner or by record type)?
clarifications.why: A dashboard component only responds to a dashboard filter if it declares dashboardFilterColumns for that field.
clarifications.answer_shape: The filter design and per-component column mapping if a filter is wanted after all.
clarifications.proposed_default: No additional filter beyond the tile itself, per the requirement's plain "dashboard tile of the pipeline by close month."

clarifications.question: Does "pipeline by close month" need historical trending (how the pipeline looked a month ago), or only the current snapshot?
clarifications.why: Historical trending only starts collecting data the day it is enabled; there is no retroactive data.
clarifications.answer_shape: Either a trend design started now (accepting a forward-only data start), or confirmation the snapshot view is sufficient.
clarifications.proposed_default: Current snapshot only — the requirement asks for a dashboard tile of the pipeline by close month, not a trend-over-time view.

clarifications.question: For the open-pipeline report, what exact number does the VP need, and what has to appear on the same row as it?
clarifications.why: Reporting requirements assume joins the report-type rules forbid; a four-object join chain is the ceiling.
clarifications.answer_shape: A reporting row naming base object (Opportunity), join chain (none beyond OpportunityLineItem if discount lives there), and whether rows with no product line must still appear.
clarifications.proposed_default: Amount and discount on the same row as Stage and Opportunity Name, per the requirement's "report of open Enterprise opportunities by stage with amount and discount."

clarifications.question: Will Enterprise Opportunity ever need more than this one approval process (e.g. a separate one for Renewal, or a future contract-terms approval)?
clarifications.why: A submission enters exactly one process; entry criteria are evaluated in the org's process order, and process order is not carried in the metadata, so a second process later becomes a manual re-ordering step in every org.
clarifications.answer_shape: The ordered process list (today: one process) plus a note that order must be re-set by hand in the target org after deploy if a second process is added later.
clarifications.proposed_default: One process, entry criteria "Discount > 20%", used by both Enterprise and Renewal opportunities per the requirement.

clarifications.question: Will this approval process ever have more than one approver on a single step (needing whenMultipleApprovers), or is it always exactly one manager?
clarifications.why: On a unanimous multi-approver step, one rejection flips every other approver's StepStatus to NoResponse rather than Rejected, which changes what the LWC's approval-status field should show.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation of single-approver-per-step, or the whenMultipleApprovers value and the status-field mapping if not.
clarifications.proposed_default: Exactly one approver per step — the requirement names a single manager approval, not a panel.

clarifications.question: If a manager rejects the approval, does the request die entirely, or can the rep resubmit after adjusting the discount?
clarifications.why: rejectBehavior (RejectRequest vs BackToPrevious) is set per step and cannot be changed once the process has been activated, even after deactivating it.
clarifications.answer_shape: The per-step reject behaviour, decided before the first activation, and confirmation the rep can simply resubmit a corrected request afterward.
clarifications.proposed_default: RejectRequest — a single-step process (rep to manager) has no prior step to return to.

clarifications.question: Should an opportunity that does not actually need approval (discount ≤ 20%) be auto-approved if it is ever routed into this process by mistake, or should it never enter the process at all?
clarifications.why: ifCriteriaNotMet is ApproveRecord, RejectRecord (first step only), or GotoNextStep; the entry criteria should mean this never happens, but the field still has to be set.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation entry criteria are the real gate, with the field set defensively.
clarifications.proposed_default: The process entry criteria (Discount > 20%) should prevent this; the field itself is not user-facing so any legal value is acceptable — default ApproveRecord.

clarifications.question: How many Enterprise/Renewal opportunities are created a day, and what is the biggest single batch anyone would ever push through this process?
clarifications.why: Automation that passes UAT on ten records fails on a large batch; this decides whether the validation rule and approval process need to consider bulk/API entry paths at all.
clarifications.answer_shape: A data_volume value with a steady-state number and a worst-case batch number.
clarifications.proposed_default: Very low volume and single-record entry — 12 reps, no integration, no data migration, per the requirement.

clarifications.question: When you say managers need to see the report — can reps not open it at all, or can they open it but should the discount/amount not be visible to them?
clarifications.why: Record access and field access are different mechanisms configured in different places, and "record access" itself is seven ordered layers.
clarifications.answer_shape: A sharing_impact value naming the layer (folder access here) plus a separate FLS row if field-level hiding is also wanted.
clarifications.proposed_default: Reps cannot open the report/dashboard folder at all, per the requirement's "Managers need a report..." wording; no field-level discount hiding is implied.

clarifications.question: Who exactly works this process — Northwind employees only, or does any partner or customer-facing portal user touch an Enterprise/Renewal opportunity?
clarifications.why: The answer selects a licence, and licence selects API allocation, object access and portal template long before design starts.
clarifications.answer_shape: A licence_implication value confirming standard Salesforce (internal) licences throughout.
clarifications.proposed_default: Employees only — 12 reps, 2 managers, 1 sales-ops admin, all named as internal roles in the requirement.

clarifications.question: Where does the discount value and the product-line data live right now — only in Salesforce, or does it originate in a quoting tool or spreadsheet?
clarifications.why: A requirement sourced from another system is an integration requirement wearing a validation-rule costume, and needs a pattern decision before sizing.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation of "Salesforce only," closing off the integration-pattern-selection branch for this build.
clarifications.proposed_default: Salesforce only — the requirement explicitly states no integrations and no data migration.

assumptions.text: Enterprise and Renewal run genuinely different stage sequences, so two Sales Processes and two Record Types are required rather than one wide process.
assumptions.because: Q36 informational, left unanswered at G1; the proposed default is applied and requirement.md item 1 names the two lists.

assumptions.text: The board pack uses the standard forecast-category vocabulary, and Q5's UI word 'Commit' is written as the metadata token 'Forecast' - the ForecastCategories enum has exactly Omitted, Pipeline, BestCase, Forecast, Closed.
assumptions.because: Q37 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied, and the UI-to-metadata mapping is grounded in admin/opportunity-management/references/gotchas.md.

assumptions.text: No integration or Apex writes Probability or ForecastCategoryName on an Enterprise or Renewal opportunity, so the stage-to-category mapping is the only source of those values.
assumptions.because: Q38 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied, consistent with requirement.md item 6.

assumptions.text: Stage field history relies on the platform default (OpportunitySettings.enableOpportunityFieldHistoryTracking defaults to true); no settings file is shipped to turn it on, and history cannot be backfilled if it turns out to be off.
assumptions.because: Q39 informational, left unanswered at G1; its default asks for history from day one but no step ships OpportunitySettings, so the default is recorded as relied-upon rather than delivered.

assumptions.text: StageName is the only picklist that differs between the two record types; no other field needs a per-record-type picklistValues block beyond Approval_Status__c, which is identical on both.
assumptions.because: Q40 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied.

assumptions.text: Person Accounts are not enabled, so no personAccountDefault element is needed on any record-type visibility block.
assumptions.because: Q41 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied.

assumptions.text: Both rules are enforced everywhere - API, every layout, Flow - because they are validation rules rather than layout-Required settings.
assumptions.because: Q42 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied.

assumptions.text: No legacy workflow field update or other existing automation writes StageName, Amount, Discount__c or Approval_Status__c after save, so the approval process's field updates are the only writer of Approval_Status__c.
assumptions.because: Q43 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied. If a legacy rule exists it would overwrite the approval status silently.

assumptions.text: Neither formula reads a compound field, a person name or a dependent picklist, so the API-20.0 compound-field prohibition on validation rules is not in play.
assumptions.because: Q44 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied.

assumptions.text: Picklist tests in the discount formula use ISPICKVAL rather than ISBLANK/ISNULL applied directly to the picklist, which is what VR-PICK-01 in check_validation_rules.py exists to catch.
assumptions.because: Q45 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied.

assumptions.text: Each record type gets its own Path, because only one path may exist per record type per object.
assumptions.because: Q46 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied and reinforced by admin/path-and-guidance/references/metadata-examples.md section 2.

assumptions.text: The target org is Sales Cloud Enterprise, where pathAssistantEnabled defaults true - the settings file still ships so the preference is explicit and survives a scratch-org or Developer-Edition build environment where it defaults false.
assumptions.because: Q47 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied.

assumptions.text: Path guidance is shipped with canOverrideAutoPathCollapseWithUserPref true so a rep's expanded path persists across records; nobody asked for guidance that cannot be collapsed at all.
assumptions.because: Q48 informational, left unanswered at G1 and carrying NO proposed default; the value is taken from admin/path-and-guidance/references/metadata-examples.md section 3, which says to ship it true unless there is a reason not to.

assumptions.text: The rep advances the stage in the UI; no automation moves StageName, which Q17's answer also forbids.
assumptions.because: Q49 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied.

assumptions.text: A new Lightning record page is built rather than editing whatever page the org has today, and it uses a template that provides the subheader region the Path component needs.
assumptions.because: Q50 informational, left unanswered at G1; the default allowed either, and building new is the option that cannot damage an existing page.

assumptions.text: Q11's 'Primary Contact with the Decision Maker contact role' is guidance text on the Propose Path step, not a key field: PathAssistantStep.fieldNames takes fields on entityName and an OpportunityContactRole is a related record.
assumptions.because: Q11 was answered, but the answer names a related record the metadata type cannot hold; recorded here rather than silently dropped.

assumptions.text: The panel runs on Lightning Experience desktop and the Salesforce mobile app only - supportedFormFactors Large and Small - with no Experience Cloud target, so lightning/platformShowToastEvent is the correct toast import.
assumptions.because: Q51 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied.

assumptions.text: The discount is displayed, never edited, in the panel; editing stays on the layout field.
assumptions.because: Q52 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied.

assumptions.text: One approval process serves both record types, entered on discount above 20%.
assumptions.because: Q58 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied.

assumptions.text: Exactly one approver per step, so whenMultipleApprovers is not set.
assumptions.because: Q59 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied.

assumptions.text: A rejection ends the request - there is one step, so there is no prior step to return to and no rejectBehavior element on it.
assumptions.because: Q60 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied, and rejectBehavior is not allowed on a first step in any case.

assumptions.text: Process entry criteria keep sub-cap discounts out of the process entirely, so no ifCriteriaNotMet path is exercised.
assumptions.because: Q61 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied.

assumptions.text: Volume is very low - 12 reps, single-record entry, no data load - so the Apex submits one record per invocation and needs no chunking.
assumptions.because: Q62 informational, left unanswered at G1; default applied and consistent with Q29's answer.

assumptions.text: The OpportunityStage standardValueSet file this build deploys must be the UNION of the org's currently active stage values and the eight new ones. A partial file deactivates every value it omits, which would strip the SMB pipeline of its stages.
assumptions.because: No retrieve is possible in a design-only build and no clarification asked for the org's current stage list; the deactivate-by-omission rule is stated in admin/picklist-and-value-sets/references/metadata-examples.md section 3.

assumptions.text: The set of standard fields the platform requires on an Opportunity page layout is unknown. Only the Case set is verified in this library, and admin/record-types-and-page-layouts/references/metadata-examples.md says outright not to extrapolate it. The two layouts carry Q20's five fields and the set is discovered by iterating scripts/mock_deploy.py --dry-run.
assumptions.because: Q20 named the fields the requester wants; the platform's own required-item set is an org fact no answer supplies.

assumptions.text: The Opportunity Products related-list API name must be copied from a retrieve of an existing Opportunity layout. The layouts ship without a relatedLists block and the deploy-order note carries the instruction.
assumptions.because: The string is in no skill in this library; admin/opportunity-management/references/metadata-examples.md says related-list names are retrieval aliases and must never be hand-authored.

assumptions.text: The rejection email points the rep at the Approval History related list rather than quoting the manager's comments, because no {!ApprovalRequest.*} merge field is documented anywhere in this library.

assumptions.text: The report's column codes are provisional Object$Field strings. They are report-type-specific, cannot be verified offline, and must be diffed against a retrieve of a working report on the same report type before deploy.
